posts.body:
Welcome to RPG MAKER GUILD
Today, we're excited to announce the launch of RPG MAKER GUILD, the new official RPG Maker forum operated by Gotcha Gotcha Games Inc..
Our goal is to provide a welcoming space where RPG Maker creators can connect, share projects, exchange ideas, and continue growing the community together. We look forward to building on the creativity, knowledge, and passion that have made the RPG Maker community so special over the years.
■Visit RPG MAKER GUILD:
https://guild.rpgmakerofficial.com/
To support the transition to the new forum, new account registrations have been disabled as of today. Beginning on June 18th, 2026 JST, posting and account-related features will be disabled and the forum will become read-only. The forum will remain accessible in read-only mode until December 11th, 2026 JST.
For details regarding the transition schedule, account information, forum data, and frequently asked questions, please see the FAQ below.
■Forum Closure FAQ:
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/threads/rpg-maker-web-forum-closure-faq.183960/
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Thank You from KOMODO
First and foremost, we would like to thank everyone who has contributed to the forum over the years. From creators sharing their games and resources to community members helping one another, your passion and support have helped make the RPG Maker community what it is today.
We are grateful to have been part of this journey and are excited to see the community continue to grow in its new home.
Thank you for your support and contributions throughout the years.
— The KOMODO Team

posts.author: Rethy
posts.body:
This is a Mass Extinction Event for the franchise no matter how you slice it. Disabling posting in a week is horrific, that is not nearly enough of a warning, but seeing that even the read-only version was going to be taken down in six months made my eyes bug out of my skull. I only hope the tsunami of backlash pushes those dates back, but I'm not counting on it.
Even before I joined the forums, it was an invaluable tool in my game development. I always had a couple of tabs open, and when I ran into verification issues when I finally did make an account it was a huge blow to my game dev at the time as I had to work off of incognito windows. But the help I was able to receive after joining was a difference in an order of a magnitude. I would post an issue that I had been banging my head against for a couple of months, and someone would post the exact solution within a couple of hours.
I am in the final leg of development. I was planning to have my game finished and released at the end of the month, I was literally working on compiling and writing out the credits when I realised this thread exists. I was counting on forum viewers to be a big part of my early player base. There's almost no chance I'll be able to finish the game before the forums go read-only, and who knows how many people with be in the mood to play a new game when that happens. I was also looking forward to paying it back in some small part by sharing the few odd assets and snippets I've put together myself over the development of my game. It sucks that while I'm in the middle of Full Crunch mode I now have to run crisis management and adapt my marketing and release plans. It's also hard to imagine many people donating much of their time and effort for help with the last bits polish when things are burning down all around them.
As much as it feels like particularly bad timing for me, the forums have been instrumental in getting my game ready for release over these past 6 months and it is almost certainly still going to be finished in the very near future and I recognize I am not even close to the worst affected by this. My heart goes out to devs who have spent years working on commercial games and earning money off of commissions whose bottom line this affects. I feel awful for people just starting work on their games or will start working on them when this is not a resource available to them. I can barely imagine being one of the people who has generously donated hundred of hours of work building this community over the past 14 years, and all those who spent critical points in their life and formed real relationships with this community.
I've gotta go figure out what I'm gonna do, but I'm hoping to see the last of my development through with this community and wish all the best for everyone here.

posts.author: Anastasius
posts.body:
Why are you guys panicking as though it's the apocalypse?
Firstly, the international RPG Maker community originally never needed corporate backing anyway. In fact, RPGM was never even supposed to leave Japan. You only have a global community because hobbyists shared bootlegs and made fan games with ripped sprites. So if a few pirates can spark an obsession with a generation of game developers through legally questionable means I'm pretty sure you guys can handle this with the legal tools you have today.
Secondly, you are  entrusting an enormous chunk of your happiness and social circle to a for-profit corporation. Obviously you're going to end up disappointed sooner or later. If RPG Maker and this forums are your sole source of happiness and social life, then life's going to be tough for you.
Thirdly, as many of you have already mentioned, GGG is tone-deaf. Begging only works if the other guy listens. In fact, by begging them for mercy you are basically telling GGG that you badly need them, and judging by their actions in the last couple of years and now, they don't really need you. In short, you "currently" don't have leverage over GGG. Put in another way, begging is a waste of time. You should do something actually productive... like setting up Discord channels and websites for the eventual forum refugees. Or if you don't like interacting with people, just download stuff here while you still can.
Fourthly, you don't need to archive the entire contents of this forum. You should prioritize the downloadable resources (assets, plugins, etc.) as well as the links to websites housing these resources (e.g. Avery's profile page). Next would be the tutorials (e.g. Avery's). The text-only remainder (support threads, game mechanics design, general lounge, etc.) should come last. Like them or not, AI bots have likely used those as training data and so will regurgitate them if you bother to ask, hallucinations and all.
Fifthly, these forums have earned a certain notoriety for toxicity to which the regulars (the people who hang around here 24/7) are tone-deaf to. You can still see this now even as the forum dies: the ad hominem attacks, the mocking reactions, the doxxing of any member of the 99% who dare offend the regulars. If the regulars remain narrow-minded and tone-deaf (much like GGG), if the regulars never learned anything from the death of these forums, then good luck to their future endeavors.
Lastly, here is a story that might inspire you: the history of the Baldur's Gate 3 wiki.
Spoiler:
History of the Baldur's Gate 3 Wiki
Before bg3.wiki existed, the main source for Baldur's Gate 3 information was hosted on Fextralife, which is still notorious for aggressive advertisements, auto-playing Twitch streams and strict copyright claims over user-written text. Basically, Fextralife owns the copyright of anything you write there, not you.
So one guy named Taylan started bg3.wiki using open-source software, funded by player donations. The goal was to build a clean, accurate and highly detailed database. Dedicated fans began populating the site with precise tables for weapons, armor and hidden game code mechanics.
When Baldur's Gate 3 fully launched in August 2023 traffic to bg3.wiki exploded. Word of mouth on Reddit and Discord turned the site into the go-to resource for millions of players. As traffic grew hosting costs skyrocketed. To keep the servers running on Hetzner Online without draining user wallets, the organizers shifted away from donations and introduced light non-intrusive advertisements.
The site remains fully independent. It currently hosts thousands highly detailed pages curated entirely by the community.
The international RPG Maker community never needed corporate backing before. If you're sick and tired of GGG's shenanigans, you can do something about it.

Now that I think about it, this situation reminds me of a Chinese cultural center that closed down.
I liked that place, I'm sure the Chinese liked that place, but in the end it was bought out and replaced with corporate hegemony. I'm not sure why takeovers have to equate to utter annihilation every time.
You can have
both
! The property and the hearts of the people!
As a fellow successful money person* (degenerate stock gambler), there has to be a way to communicate the benefits of keeping the forum alive. Because it is about finances at the end of the day.
So, the new hands want people to migrate to the new place, for fine reasons I'm sure.
But that doesn't mean this place has to die for it, and it shouldn't.
If I were in charge of the money, here's why I would keep this forum.
I would say I'm fairly unbiased because I'm not a regular here, so I'm not speaking from emotion.
---
+
SEO: Search Engine Optimization
This place is one of the best known RPG Maker resources.
Why get rid of a secure spot in the algorithm?
Especially in this age where it will be harder to get your name in lights, with the advent of AI?
+
Established Community
To hype your products, you need a congregation of likeminded individuals.
The people here have worked on RPG Maker for decades.
A niche though it may be, I don't think it's a good idea to scatter the loyal customers.
Splitting the consensus just gets you less consensus.
There will always be hermits who will keep to the same website; the userbase won't all migrate to the new place, some of them will just disappear. After all, the new website might just get unceremoniously thrown in the bin again if the owners get bored, so why bother?
RPG Maker has a strong history. You need a strong throughline.
The community is the spine that holds it all together.
+
Haven
The new website could be unavailable for unforeseen reasons, be it technical issues, a hack, etc.
This forum would be a good fallback. Twitter will only help so much.
Discord is too private for the general public and casuals.
---
In summary, it is strategical to keep the forum for long-term overhead rather than looking at whatever costs may be saved right now. I can't imagine the forum is expensive enough to sacrifice the potential ramifications of isolating the community that took so long to build.
Remember, we don't exist in a vacuum. Remind yourself of the Butterfly Effect.
For me, this place has always just been around, so if I wanted to check out anything RPG Maker I'd go here. I'm open to giving the new place a chance...with the expectation that the plug can be pulled at any time. It happened to GameMaker, which makes it impossible to invest in whatever communal feature they promise because they end up having finite shelf lives.

posts.author: redgamehunter
posts.body:
I am not an active forum user, but... for several years now, I've considered RPG Maker a sub-standard piece of software, even for making RPGs specifically. Its buggy, lacks basic features that you would expect even for the years each version released, etc. The one thing that ever,
EVER
balanced it out were the forums and community resources (art, plugins, knowledge, etc.). When talking with someone about what to try out as a new dev, I still suggested RPG Maker almost every time, especially since, historically, it wasn't that hard to officially purchase old versions for those who couldn't afford the latest release, and because of these resources.
I've heard via a news site and a machine translated tweet that you guys are actually bothering to archive now, which is nice if true (far too tired this morning to dig into it yet), but, bluntly? The fact that you came out and did this at all severs all remaining goodwill I had for this ecosystem. I want this understood: even ignoring any other potential controversies that are present, to have
EVER
come out and said "For reasons we aren't going to explain in detail, we are deleting over a decade of community knowledge and resources." shows a casual contempt for the very community that's carried this software for years that I struggle to imagine. Furthermore... it shows a lack of understanding of what's even valuable about your own product. I've seen, on more than one occasion, someone be convinced to purchase your software explicitly because of the long running, active, generally well maintained forums.
Every time RPG Maker comes up in the future when I speak with a burgeoning developer, I will inform them of this moment. I will no longer be buying new versions of the software when it comes out to tinker with and support the ecosystem financially out of a hope of continued improvement.
A final note: if this is the quality with which you treat your community, made up heavily of your customer base... why should a customer feel comfortable buying from you? You can promise the world in customer support and company attention to issues right now, but you've now shown yourselves to be, ultimately, flippant and uncaring towards things that don't directly affect profits (though I'd argue the indirect positive effect on profits of this forum is much higher than you're guessing). It's a profound loss of faith you caused, for no
good
reason.

posts.author: SoulHero
posts.body:
It's weird living through a moment that will 100% be immortalized in internet history as one of its dumbest decisions.
For those in the future who are curious and just need a tl;dr, the RPG Maker community got blindsided and bamboozled by greedy corporate overlords.
People much smarter and more experienced than me can give you the bigger details; you probably already read them just to get to this point. It's just sad that despite how so many things have changed, so many things are still the same.
So, if you ever feel like making any corporation into a villian in your game or story is a massive cliché, just know that it will never go out of style. The corporations themselves won't allow it to. Hopefully, one day...it will be.
When I do finish my first game, I'm gonna dedicate it to this forum. For everyone that made it what it is.
You all deserved better, but this is the least I could do to say...thank you. For everything.
